founded.value: 2019 (as Revorf; renamed AOI Biosciences in January 2025)

growth_signal.value: Its antibody test is already used in over 300 medical institutions in Japan, and it is expanding into Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan and Indonesia; a cited clinical study found treated patients had over double the pregnancy rate and 1.7 times the live-birth rate of untreated patients.

raised.note: confirmed by two sources in the run; the URLs were not saved
raised.value: About ¥500M in a September 2026 round (new shares plus a secondary share sale), bringing cumulative funding to about ¥1 billion

entry.idea: AOI Biosciences tests blood for a specific antibody linked to infertility and repeated miscarriage, so doctors can identify at-risk patients and treat them before trying to conceive.
entry.lesson: Pairing a single, well-validated diagnostic test with a larger drug discovery platform lets a company generate near-term revenue while it builds out a longer-term research bet.
entry.name: AOI Biosciences

growth.reason: The test is already adopted by over 300 hospitals in Japan and is expanding into four more Asian countries, with strong clinical outcome data behind it.

market.reason: Infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss affect many couples worldwide, though this specific antibody test addresses only a fraction of those cases.

tech.reason: Combining a validated antibody diagnostic with quantum-inspired protein structure prediction, developed jointly with Toshiba, is genuinely novel science that would take real time to replicate.

entry.twist: It also uses quantum-inspired computing, developed with Toshiba, to predict hidden control points on proteins that could become new drug targets, an approach it applies to its own drug discovery research.
entry.who_pays: Hospitals and clinics pay to run AOI's antibody test on patients, and pharmaceutical partners may eventually pay to license its drug discovery technology.
entry.why_now: About one fifth of recurrent pregnancy loss cases have no known cause, and a validated blood test that identifies one specific antibody gives doctors a concrete, actionable diagnosis where none existed before.

mentions.snippet: Antibody tests and drug research for infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss; about ¥500M raised.
